subject: SLO credit allocation + rolling maintenance window redlines — legal coordination
messages:
From: Alisha Patel <alisha.patel@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2025-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on uptime/credits and maintenance carveouts

Hi Naomi / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Legal at Acme flagged a few items we need clarified before we can move to counters:

- The uptime target in the order form (99.9%) — we need to understand the calculation window and whether regional outages count toward the global SLA.
- Service credits cap appears to be 50% of monthly fees; our procurement team prefers a per-incident cap to avoid exposure from multi-day incidents.
- Maintenance: the draft allows rolling maintenance with 8-hour notification. We need firm blackout periods for our payroll cutover (first week of any month) and agreed advance notice for major version upgrades.

Can you confirm how credits are calculated (per-incident vs monthly aggregate), and whether you can commit to maintenance blackout windows and a stricter notification for major upgrades? I attached our standard procurement questionnaire for reference.

Best,
Alisha Patel
Sr Procurement Lead, Acme Cloud
Attachment: Acme_Procurement_Q.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alisha Patel <alisha.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-18T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on uptime/credits and maintenance carveouts

Alisha — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline and next steps below.

- Uptime calculation: We measure uptime per customer across the region(s) the customer pins in the Order Form. For multi-region customers we can offer both regional and combined availability metrics; the Order Form currently references combined. If you prefer regional-only triggers, we can add a clause to scope by region.

- Credit cap: The default order form uses an aggregate monthly cap (50% of monthly recurring charges). We can propose an alternative per-incident cap (e.g., 25% per incident, up to 75% monthly) — this is negotiable, but would like to confirm your preference so we can surface to Legal.

- Maintenance blackout windows: We can add fixed blackout windows (example: first 00:00–06:00 UTC on the 1st of month) as an exclusion for rolling maintenance. For major upgrades (semantic version changes or migration requiring node restarts >30s), we can commit to a 21-day notice and a scheduled maintenance playbook.

Attaching our suggested redline bundle and a candidate SLO credit matrix (slo-credit-matrix.xlsx).

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether you want regional-scoped SLOs or global-combined.
2) Confirm preferred credit model (per-incident cap vs monthly aggregate and numerical caps).
3) If blackout windows are required, send specific times/dates (we'll put into Order Form as carveouts).

Happy to set a 30-min call with Legal & Ops if helpful.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Principal Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Acme_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf; slo-credit-matrix.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-07-19T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on uptime/credits and maintenance carveouts

Alisha — quick commercial note as you consider the tradeoffs:

- Per-incident cap: we can do 25% per incident with a 75% monthly cap (keeps total risk bounded while allowing meaningful per-event remediation).
- Regional SLOs: if Acme wants region-specific SLOs, pricing will reflect the operational cost of pinning capacity and separate runbooks — can provide a delta estimate.
- Blackouts: we can accept fixed blackout windows for specific payroll cutovers but would ask for a quarterly exception window (two 4-hour outages maximum outside scheduled blackout) to allow critical security patching if needed.

If you agree in principle to the numbers above, we'll prep a formal counter and loop in Legal.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarification on uptime/credits and maintenance carveouts

Looping in Legal/Service Ops perspective and proposing concrete redline language (see excerpt below). Quoted for context:

"On Fri, Jul 18, 2025 at 9:12 AM Alisha Patel <alisha.patel@acme.com> wrote:
> The uptime target in the order form (99.9%) — we need to understand the calculation window and whether regional outages count toward the global SLA.
> Service credits cap appears to be 50% of monthly fees; our procurement team prefers a per-incident cap to avoid exposure from multi-day incidents.
> Maintenance: the draft allows rolling maintenance with 8-hour notification. We need firm blackout periods for our payroll cutover (first week of any month) and agreed advance notice for major version upgrades.

Proposed legal-friendly redlines:
- "Availability measurement": "Availability shall be measured per region designated in the Order Form. For multi-region deployments, Customer may elect regional or aggregate availability in the Order Form; the elected scope determines credit eligibility."
- "Credit calculation": "Service Credit for an eligible incident shall be calculated per incident as a percentage of the monthly recurring charges for the service impacted, up to 25% per incident. Customer may accrue credits with a monthly cap equal to 75% of monthly recurring charges."
- "Maintenance exclusions and blackout windows": "Customer may designate up to four blackout windows per 12-month period (each window up to 6 hours) during which scheduled maintenance shall not be performed. For major upgrades (as defined by a change in major version or disruptive platform migration), Redwood will provide at least 21 calendar days' written notice and a rollback plan."

Operational asks: we need your payroll blackout dates (or reccurring rule). Also confirm whether Acme wants regional SLOs elected on the Order Form.

If these redlines look acceptable I will produce a tracked-change MSA and supplemental Order Form for signatures.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Contracts & Platform Ops, Redwood Inference

- Availability scope: Acme elects to measure availability per-region in the Order Form (please confirm region list).
- Credits: Redwood proposes 25% per-incident cap, 75% monthly aggregate cap (Karthik will add tracked changes).
- Blackout windows: Acme to provide recurring payroll blackout rule (we suggest: first business day of each month, 02:00–06:00 local timezone) or specific calendar dates; Redwood will mark those as scheduled-exclusion windows in the Order Form. Major upgrades get 21-day notice and rollback plan.
